Looping you both for a quick sanity check — Devon asked for a MAP + tokens/$ sheet for ScribeHealth (pilot ~300k calls/mo). They want the doc by Friday. Draft assumptions below (very rough):

- Model: redwood-open-13B (quantized) used for pilot; typical prompt 350 tokens, expected generation ~450 tokens -> avg 800 tokens per request.
- Hosted unit cost (current quote for redwood-open-13B): $3.20 per 1M tokens (input+output combined).
- Baseline monthly tokens: 300k * 800 = 240M tokens -> baseline cost = 240 * $3.20 = $768.
- Caching: expected prefix reuse for templated prompts; optimistic hit-rate 30% on input tokens, reducing net tokens by ~20% overall.
- Batching: with a 25 ms batching window we can get average batch size ~4. Effective compute reduction ~15% for same throughput.

Quick asks: please validate the tokens per request (Neha), confirm kernel/throughput assumptions / batching latency trade-offs (Karthik), and flag any redlines for the MAP timeline (Hannah). I attached a working sheet link for you to update.

Thanks — I want to send a version to Devon with clear conservative + stretch scenarios.

—Markus

Markus — quick validation and a couple of adjustments:

1) Tokens per request: our sampling on similar customers shows a median of ~650 tokens (prompt 300 / gen 350). Your 800 is on the higher side for ScribeHealth UX; use 700 as conservative, 900 as stretch.

2) Unit pricing: the $3.20/M you listed aligns with hosted list for this quantized variant, but include a second column for Dedicated quote (reserved capacity) where effective unit cost drops to ~$2.10/M at their projected volume. We'll present both since customers often care about committed vs on-demand economics.

3) Caching: assume 25% input-token hit rate for conservative (not 30%). That translates to ~12% net token reduction overall (input is ~40% of total tokens). For an optimistic case use 35% hit -> ~18% overall reduction.

4) Batching: kernel-level throughput gains are workload-dependent. For short sequences (avg 700 tokens) and a 20-40ms batching window we see average batch sizes 3–6; use batch size = 4 for conservative -> ~10% compute savings; optimistic batch size = 6 -> ~18% savings. Note: batching improves compute utilization but adds ~10–30ms median tail depending on routing — call out as SLO trade-off.

Synthesis (conservative):
- avg tokens/request = 700
- monthly tokens = 300k * 700 = 210M
- hosted cost = 210 * $3.20 = $672
- caching (conservative) -> -12% = ~184.8M tokens -> cost = $591
- batching (conservative) -> additional ~10% compute reduction effective -> tokens ~166.3M -> cost = ~$532

I'll update the spreadsheet with a conservative / mid / optimistic tab and add notes about latency trade-offs. Also adding an action item list for the MAP (hook we need from Scribe: representative prompt set + expected concurrency profile).

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Product Manager, Cost & Ops, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 24 May 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: MAP + unit-econ packet for ScribeHealth (attached)

Devon — attached is a concise MAP + unit economics packet: scribe_map_v2.xlsx (three scenarios: conservative / expected / optimistic) and a short note (unit_econ_note.pdf) summarizing assumptions. Key highlights below (please read the packet for full detail):

Conservative scenario (recommended for procurement):
- avg tokens/request: 700
- projected monthly tokens (pilot): 210M -> hosted cost @ $3.20/M = $672/month
- expected savings after caching (25% hit on input) and batching (avg batch size 4): net cost ~= $532/month
- Dedicated reserved capacity estimate: ~$440/month at similar traffic (requires a 6–12 month commit; exact discounted units in the spreadsheet)

Notes on trade-offs:
- Quality gating: keep generation cap at 600 tokens for pilot; we'll provide an eval prompt set + gold responses to track MRR-quality and false-positive rates.
- Latency SLOs: batching window 25ms expected median add; we recommend ScribeHealth set 200ms P95 SLO for the two-week eval (we can tighten later for Dedicated).
- Required deliverables from Scribe: representative 200–300 prompt samples, expected peak concurrency, and PO/finance contact for procurement.

Proposed MAP / close timeline:
- May 26: Scribe provides prompt sample + PO contact
- Jun 3: pilot environment deployed (private dataset subset)
- Jun 10–16: 2-week eval window (quality + unit-econ verification)
- Jun 17–23: internal review / procurement cycle
- Jun 26: targeted signature (legal/finance) and go/no-go

Action items (owners):
- Scribe: send prompt sample + procurement contact (Devon)
- Redwood (Neha): finalize econ sheet & add Dedicated pricing row (done)
- Redwood (Karthik): finalize pilot infra runbook + latency checklist (in progress)
- Markus: schedule 30-minute sync next week to review MAP with Scribe and procurement.

Attachments: scribe_map_v2.xlsx (pricing scenarios + detailed token calc), unit_econ_note.pdf (assumptions + gating checklist). HubSpot deal link included for reference.

Would you like me to include a short line-item for potential overage credits if pilot spikes beyond projections? I can propose a one-time buffer credit to smooth procurement concerns.

Best —
